item.title: DARP: Durable Activity Record Protocol
item.content:encoded: I created DARP so coding agents can send meaningful work records to Factory Log through a small, open protocol without surveillance.

item.title: Use 1Password Developer Environments with Cursor
item.content:encoded: Learn how the 1Password Cursor plugin mounts secrets without plaintext .env files, what its skill and validation hook do, and how to use it safely.

item.title: A deep dive into T3 Code
item.content:encoded: Learn how T3 Code runs Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok, and OpenCode through one local web, desktop, and mobile control plane.

item.title: A deep dive into 1Password Developer Environments
item.content:encoded: Learn how 1Password Developer Environments store, share, mount, and inject project secrets, including their security model and practical limits.

item.title: Introduction to Docker Compose
item.content:encoded: Introduction to Docker Compose: run multi-container apps from one file, with services, volumes, ports, and a Node plus Postgres example.

item.title: Build and ship real software with AI
item.content:encoded: The September 2026 Bootcamp is a 10-week, beginner-friendly program for building and shipping real software with AI coding agents.

item.title: A deep dive into StyleX
item.content:encoded: Learn how StyleX turns JavaScript style objects into regular CSS classes at build time, with React and Astro setup, variants, themes, and responsive styles.

item.title: A deep dive into GitHub Actions
item.content:encoded: A practical deep dive into GitHub Actions: workflows, runners, job graphs, artifacts, caching, security, deployments, and debugging.

item.title: A deep dive into hey-cli
item.content:encoded: hey-cli brings HEY email, contacts, calendars, todos, habits, time tracking, journal entries, automation, and AI agent workflows to your terminal.

item.title: A deep dive into Ponytail
item.content:encoded: Learn how Ponytail stops AI coding agents from over-engineering: install it in ChatGPT, Codex, or Claude Code, choose a mode, and review diffs.

item.title: How to exit, close, and detach from Herdr
item.content:encoded: Learn the difference between detaching, closing a pane, stopping a session, and exiting Herdr without accidentally killing running work.

item.title: Build an idempotent scheduled job with Cloudflare Queues and D1
item.content:encoded: Build a reliable Cloudflare scheduled job with Queues and D1, using stable work IDs, expiring leases, safe retries, and fixed cadence.

item.title: A deep dive into Cursor Origin
item.content:encoded: Cursor Origin hosts Git repositories inside Cursor. Learn how its repos, GitHub sync, pull requests, agents, apps, CLI, and early-beta limits work.

item.title: Using Herdr from a phone
item.content:encoded: Connect to a persistent Herdr session from a phone over SSH, use the narrow-screen interface, and safely check running coding agents.

item.title: How to use zoxide
item.content:encoded: Learn how to install and set up zoxide, then jump between frequently used directories with z, interactive selection, and frecency ranking.

item.title: How to send email with Cloudflare Email Service
item.content:encoded: Send transactional email from a Cloudflare Worker using the native Email Service binding, with domain setup, local testing, and error handling.

item.title: A deep dive into Nurb
item.content:encoded: Nurb turns a coding agent into a CAD partner. Learn how Python parts, OCCT solids, live checks, measurements, and 3MF export fit together.

item.title: Modern CSS colors: oklch() and color-mix()
item.content:encoded: oklch() gives perceptually uniform colors, and color-mix() blends them. Build palettes and tints with modern CSS color functions in all major browsers.

item.title: Why I use anti-slop skills
item.content:encoded: Anti-slop skills catch common AI habits before they reach the final result. Here's how I use them as a separate review pass for writing and code.

item.title: Herdr vs tmux vs Zellij
item.content:encoded: Compare Herdr, tmux, and Zellij for persistent terminal sessions, remote work, layouts, plugins, and running multiple coding agents.

item.title: Scroll-driven CSS animations
item.content:encoded: Animate elements from scroll position with animation-timeline scroll() and view(). No JavaScript needed. Check current browser support before shipping.

item.title: Swamp tutorial: make AI agent work repeatable
item.content:encoded: Learn how Swamp turns one-off AI agent work into typed, repeatable automation with models, workflows, assertions, and versioned data.

item.title: How to group array items with Object.groupBy()
item.content:encoded: Group an array by a property with Object.groupBy() instead of a reduce loop. See a realistic expense example and Map.groupBy() for object keys.

item.title: A deep dive into Grok Bot
item.content:encoded: A detailed Grok Bot guide covering setup, persistent computers, skills, routines, templates, approvals, real use cases, limits, pricing, and alternatives.

item.title: A practical guide to Herdr plugins
item.content:encoded: Install, inspect, configure, run, and build Herdr plugins, with practical commands and the security checks to make before trusting one.

item.title: CSS Subgrid
item.content:encoded: CSS subgrid lets nested grid items align to parent tracks. Build aligned cards and forms, understand spans and gaps, and add a practical fallback.

item.title: A deep dive into pstack
item.content:encoded: pstack is a Cursor plugin for rigorous agent work. The same SKILL.md files also load in Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents.

item.title: How to use Herdr skills and herdr --skill
item.content:encoded: Learn how to install the Herdr agent skill, use herdr --skill, and let coding agents safely inspect, split, run, and wait in panes.

item.title: JavaScript immutable array methods: toSorted(), toReversed(), toSpliced(), with()
item.content:encoded: Need to sort or reverse an array without mutating it? Use toSorted(), toReversed(), toSpliced(), and with() to get a new copy instead.

item.title: Native CSS Nesting
item.content:encoded: Native CSS nesting works without Sass. Learn basic nesting, the ampersand selector, nested media queries, specificity gotchas, and when to drop preprocessors.
